verdict.classification: real TypeGPU CPU defect (not a harness/specification issue)

confirmedDefects.title: CPU integer multiplication goes through JS Number (f64) and loses low bits when the exact product exceeds 2^53
operations: operator `*` on integer vectors inside a 'use gpu' function run on the CPU
d.i32(std.mul(a, b)) / d.u32(std.mul(a, b)) on scalars
confirmedDefects.cause: packages/typegpu/src/std/operators.ts cpuMul -> generalizeFn((a, b) => a * b) (f64 multiply) -> vec constructor -> castElement = i32/u32 schema -> `v | 0` / `(v & 0xffffffff) >>> 0` on the already-rounded double

expectedSpecificationDifferences.what: std.intdiv (scalars): CPU follows its documented formula trunc(trunc(a)/trunc(b)); GPU follows WGSL integer division
std.div / std.mod on integer vectors: GPU = WGSL integer rules for every lane; CPU is correct wherever it does not throw; CPU throws FiniteMathAssumptionError on a zero divisor
scalar i32/u32 are plain JS numbers on the CPU (no wrap-around without an explicit cast) — by design, see reports/report.json known divergences

unsupported.what: std.intdiv on integer vectors is rejected by TypeGPU (signature accepts i32/u32 scalars only)

unverifiedHypotheses.what: Scalar std.div / std.mod on integers are compiled to f32 operations (observed in emitted WGSL); their GPU precision above 2^24 and zero-divisor behaviour were not investigated further here

Impact on user code that emulates integer hashes/PRNGs on the CPU with `*` on u32 vectors: demonstrated for a PCG/Knuth-style multiplier on random u32 states, not demonstrated on any real TypeGPU user code
Other CPU paths that might multiply through f64 (e.g. matrices of integers do not exist in WGSL; compound `*=` operators; std functions built on mul) were not enumerated
